To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lipids regulate the bidirectional transport of apoB in polarized enterocyte Caco-2 monolayers.
lipids regulate the intracellular traffic and the secretion of apoB in polarized enterocytic cells.
lipids control the bidirectional traffic of a secreted protein in polarized enterocytic cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms that control the intracellular trafficking and secretion of apoB, a major secretory protein in enterocytes.
the control of apo B traffic in enterocytes, and more generally in polarized cells.
the study of lipid-dependent intracellular trafficking of apoB.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
apoB traffic is controlled by a dynamic process that involves the apical supply of lipids and cholesterol, the apical presence of complex lipid micelle and a microtubular network.

apoB is a lipid-dependent secretory protein that is transported from the endoplasic reticulum to the apical membrane and that, once there, its secretion is controlled by the presence of lipidic complexes at the apical surface of enterocytes.
the lipids in the lumen of the small intestine are the major determinants that control the traffic and secretion of apoB.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lipids control the traffic of apoB from its synthesis to its secretion.
apoB is a lipid-dependent protein that can be secreted in both apical and basolateral directions in polarized enterocyte-like Caco-2 cell line.
lipids are required for the intracellular traffic and secretion of apoB in the enterocyte.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lipids are able to modulate the intracellular traffic and secretion of a secretory apoprotein in a polarized cell.
the intracellular traffic and the secretion of apoB in polarized enterocyte cells are under the control of lipids, and that this control is dependent upon the polarity of the cells.
the lipid content of the apical and basolateral compartments controls the intracellular traffic and apical and baso-lateral secretion of apoB.
